layers.title: Sea-ice thickness, monthly mean (GLORYS12)
layers.source: Mercator Ocean GLORYS12V1 1/12° ocean–sea-ice reanalysis, via Copernicus Marine (C2)
layers.method: Model reanalysis with data assimilation (not a direct observation). Shown where concentration ≥ 15 %. Southern limit 80° S. Sub-sampled to 1/6°.

layers.title: Sea-ice concentration uncertainty: multi-reanalysis ensemble spread
layers.source: Copernicus Marine global ocean ensemble reanalysis, mean & standard deviation product (C3)
layers.method: Standard deviation of monthly sea-ice concentration across the reanalysis ensemble members — a measure of disagreement, not an error bar against observations.

layers.title: Sea-ice concentration, monthly mean (OSI SAF climate record)
layers.source: EUMETSAT OSI SAF OSI-450-a CDR + OSI-430-a ICDR, via Copernicus Marine (C1)
layers.method: Monthly mean of daily passive-microwave concentration; cells below 15 % are transparent. Days with missing swaths are excluded.

layers.title: Sea-ice concentration from SAR + AMSR2 (DMI ASIP, ML-03 test dates)
layers.source: DMI ASIP automated sea-ice product (Sentinel-1 SAR + AMSR2), 1 km, via Copernicus Marine (C4)
layers.method: Daily analysis on the ML-03 test-scene dates (dates with almost no valid data are skipped); averaged from 0.025° to 0.1° for the globe. Cells below 15 % are transparent. Swath gaps leave holes.

layers.title: Sea-ice drift: monthly mean speed and direction
layers.source: IFREMER / CERSAT AMSR-E + AMSR2 3-day sea-ice drift (P3D), via Copernicus Marine (C5)
layers.method: Colour: monthly mean of daily drift speed. Arrows (2023 onwards): monthly-mean drift vector; 0.1 m/s ≈ 150 km arrow. Passive-microwave drift is unreliable in summer melt.

layers.title: Near-surface ocean temperature anomaly vs 1993–2020 (MULTIOBS)
layers.source: Copernicus Marine MULTIOBS global ocean T/S reconstruction from in-situ and satellite observations (C7)
layers.method: Monthly near-surface temperature minus the 1993–2020 mean of the same calendar month. Under sea ice, values are mostly interpolated from sparse profiles.

layers.title: 2 m air temperature anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: Mean sea-level pressure anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: Sea-surface temperature anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: 2 m air temperature, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Absolute daily-mean temperature for the latest 92 days available on disk.

layers.title: Sea-ice thickness, merged CryoSat-2 + Sentinel-3 + SMOS (weekly samples)
layers.source: AWI merged sea-ice thickness (CryoSat-2, Sentinel-3A/B altimetry + SMOS L-band), ESA product via Copernicus Marine (C6)
layers.method: Daily L4 optimal-interpolation analysis; one field every 7 days is shown. Altimetry constrains thick ice, SMOS thin ice. Antarctic snow-depth assumptions dominate the uncertainty.

layers.title: 850 hPa temperature anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: 500 hPa geopotential height anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: Precipitation anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid. Precipitation is a model forecast field, the least constrained ERA5 variable over Antarctica.

layers.title: Total cloud cover anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid.

layers.title: Sea-ice concentration anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Monthly mean minus the 1991–2020 mean of the same calendar month. 0.25° grid. ERA5 sea ice is the OSI SAF-based boundary condition, not an independent observation. Changes smaller than 2 % are transparent.

layers.title: 10 m wind speed anomaly vs 1991–2020 (ERA5, monthly)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 monthly averaged reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store
layers.method: Speed of the monthly-mean 10 m wind vector minus its 1991–2020 calendar-month mean. Speed of the mean vector is lower than mean speed in variable winds.

layers.title: 850 hPa air temperature, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk. Over the high plateau the 850 hPa surface is below ground and values are extrapolated.

layers.title: 500 hPa geopotential height, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk. Lows (troughs) in blue, ridges in red: the westerly jet lies where the colours change fastest.

layers.title: Mean sea-level pressure, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk. Over the ice sheet sea-level pressure is a reduction to a fictitious sea level and should not be read literally.

layers.title: Total cloud cover, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk.

layers.title: Total precipitation, daily total (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk. Daily total estimated from four 6-hourly samples (00/06/12/18 UTC × 24); a model forecast field. Below 0.2 mm/day is transparent.

layers.title: Sea-ice concentration, daily (ERA5 boundary condition)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Daily values for the latest 92 days available on disk. ERA5 prescribes sea ice from OSI SAF; this is not an independent observation. Below 15 % is transparent.

layers.title: 10 m wind speed and direction, daily mean (ERA5)
layers.source: ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis aggregated to daily means (Copernicus CDS), 0.5° grid
layers.method: Speed of the daily-mean 10 m wind vector; arrows show direction (10 m/s ≈ 140 km). Katabatic winds flow off the plateau toward the coast.
